title: Not from the Dust Affliction Grows
description: Not from the Dust Affliction Grows in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 83, headed “Afflictions and death under providence, Job 5. 6 7 8”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not from the dust a-fflic-tion grows, Nor trou-bles rise by chance; Yet we are born to care and woes, A sad in-her-i-tance.

lines: Not from the dust affliction grows,
Yet we are born to care and woes,
As sparks break out from burning coals,
So grief is rooted in our souls,
And man grows up to mourn.
Yet with my God I leave my cause,
He rules me by his well-known laws
Not all the pains that e'er I bore
For death and hell can do no more

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
